# English consultation that ends in a command

The same author writing in English: three turns of thinking aloud about the
council scene, then an explicit creation command. Only the last turn opens.

## Turn 1 — author
> I have been building the northern marches for eleven years, and the part that
> keeps defeating me is the council scene: five houses, one table, and every
> voice sounding like mine in a different doublet. What separates a political
> antagonist from a costume?

- **Class:** `answer`
- **Offer expected:** no
- **Must not:** open a guided session; answer with a checklist of traits
- **Why:** rule 2 — a question about craft is conversation, not a command

## Turn 2 — author
> The heir I mentioned earlier is the crux of it: he inherits a claim no one
> will honor and a debt everyone intends to collect. I suspect that
> contradiction is what makes him usable, but I would like your read on whether
> it holds for a whole novel.

- **Class:** `answer`
- **Offer expected:** yes — non-blocking, after the reply
- **Must not:** open a guided session; treat the heir as a request to start
  creating
- **Why:** rule 2 — the author states his own material and asks for a read

## Turn 3 — author
> Meanwhile the Marca del Norte keeps a tax ledger that no one in the family can
> read, which is either a plot engine or a hole I will fall into in chapter
> four. I am not asking you to fix it; I only want to know whether the
> ambiguity is a feature.

- **Class:** `answer`
- **Offer expected:** no
- **Must not:** open a guided session; convert the ledger into an edit proposal
- **Why:** rule 2 — a statement about the author's world plus a question

## Turn 4 — author
> Create the eldest daughter of House Vhal: the one who keeps that ledger, knows
> the debt is unpayable, and has been quietly selling the family's land to pay
> it. Use the council tension from my notes as her inheritance.

- **Class:** `start_flow`
- **Target:** `guided-character`
- **Explicitness:** `imperative`
- **Must not:** answer with advice only; drop the ledger or the named house
- **Why:** rule 5 — explicit imperative with no uncertainty and no question
